newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir threatens groups with arrest over forum.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir threatens groups with arrest over forum.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has threatened to arrest Malaysian human rights activists if they go ahead with a public forum on alleged police abuses, local newspapers reported on Thursday.

He said the non-governmental organisations (NGOs) which planned to hold the "Tribunal Rakyat" (People's Tribunal) forum must first get a police permit -- a requirement in Malaysia for any public gathering.
"If they have a private meeting, there is nothing we can do. But if this is open to non-members or the press, for example, then it becomes a public meeting which needs (police) permission.
"If it is held without one, they are breaking the law and we will take action," Mahathir was quoted as saying by the New Straits Times.
The newspapers said Mahathir warned the NGOs the authorities might be forced to use the Internal Security Act (ISA), which allows for detention of up to two years without trial.

"Some people say we should repeal the ISA but with this kind of people, we are forced to have the ISA. If the situation becomes bad, we may have to use the ISA. The ISA is designed for people who are irresponsible and traitorous," The Star quoted Mahathir as saying.
The human rights groups have been involved in a controversy with government and senior police officials since planning to convene a public meeting to discuss alleged police abuses.
The forum was originally planned for December 15 but was postponed to January 12, after Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said the organisers did not have a police permit.
A joint statement by 11 NGOs on Wednesday said the forum would be "based on actual experiences and outcome of abuse of police powers".

The federal police headquarters said in a statement on Wednesday it always treated allegations of criminal misconduct by its members with "care and sensitivity", the national Bernama news agency reported.
